question: What was the loss ratio for each product in Q2 2026?

input.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT DISTINCT claim_id, payment_date, amount, payee_type FROM claim_payments), paid AS (SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) paid FROM p GROUP BY 1), inc AS (SELECT c.product, sum(coalesce(paid.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount) incurred, count(*) n FROM claims c LEFT JOIN paid USING(claim_id) WHERE c.loss_date BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY 1), ep AS (SELECT product, sum(earned_premium) ep FROM exposure_monthly WHERE month BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-06-01' GROUP BY 1) SELECT inc.product, inc.n claims, round(incurred,2) incurred, round(ep,2) earned_premium, round(incurred/ep,4) loss_ratio FROM inc JOIN ep USING(product) ORDER BY 1

report.interpretation: Loss ratio is incurred (paid plus reserve) divided by earned premium. I counted claims by loss date in Q2 2026 (2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30) and used the matching earned premium from exposure_monthly for April to June. I dropped exact-duplicate payment rows. Q2 ended three months before the extract date, so it is mostly complete. Late-reported claims, especially bodily injury and liability, may still add a little.
report.answer: Q2 2026 loss ratios: auto 53.6% and home 59.9%. Auto had 643 claims with $4.03M incurred against $7.52M earned premium. Home had 461 claims with $6.52M incurred against $10.89M earned premium.

data_quality_issues.issue: 159 payment rows were loaded twice in the out-of-batch load reload-2026-03-14. Those payments are dated 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13.
data_quality_issues.impact: None for Q2 losses. I removed exact-duplicate payment rows anyway, so the figures don't double count.

data_quality_issues.issue: Recent loss months are still filling in because claims are reported late.
data_quality_issues.impact: Q2 incurred may rise slightly as late claims arrive. Reserves are estimates, so the ratios will move as claims develop.

proposed_actions.title: Remove duplicate rows from the reload-2026-03-14 payment load
proposed_actions.reason: 159 payment rows duplicate existing payments and would overstate paid amounts for March 2026 losses.
